producer_report.summary: Adds per-gate counters and the relax/remove prevention kinds. A gate (a failed check, the verifier when no check failed, or an admission rule) counts the jobs it ended ("ends") and the times a later "try again on <job>" landed the same change ("disagreements", at most one per ended job). "Same change" means equal candidate fingerprints when both candidates share a base fingerprint, otherwise equal non-empty sorted change lists; this signal is an estimate and the docs say so. The counts feed three places. (1) The introspection prompt gets a `gate_counts` array. The schema enum gains relax and remove plus a required nullable `gate`. The system prompt now lists five kinds and says a rule or check can be wrong. (2) `apply_answer` accepts relax/remove only for a counted gate with ends >= 1 and disagreements >= 1, and stores `[gate: NAME] ` at the start of `prevention`; any other answer is a Failed record that queues nothing. (3) Hestia's `error_review` queues one normal-priority request per open gate, with the line `Gate under review: NAME.` and the counts, via new `gate_request`, `open_gate_request` and `Athena::gate_review`. `athena status` prints a "gates" section, most overruled first (JSON `gate_counts`, omitted when empty). Relax/remove records are kept out of `cause_key`, the default-proposal cases in `read_records`, retry seeds, and the producer's class summaries, so nothing asks a producer to weaken its own check. Old records are unchanged (byte round-trip test). Docs (defaults-loop.md section 3.8) and the CHANGELOG are updated. No gate is relaxed and no governance file is touched.

open_issues: Departure from the deliverable list, as the plan decided: crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs (retry_introspection and retry_cause skip relax/remove) and crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs (class_summaries skips them) are edited, each with one filter and one test, so loosening text never reaches a producer. proposals.rs is untouched.
Open question from the plan, not settled: whether a later green rerun or a verifier pass of the same change should also count as a gate disagreement. Only the unchanged-landing signal is counted.
Open question: the queued gate request lists only `crates/` and `docs/` as files (this job must not touch governance files); a reviewer may need athena.toml or defaults.toml to act on it.
Open question: a closed gate request does not stop a new one for the same gate; only one open request per gate and one per introspection id are enforced.
`athena status --snapshot` (snapshot.rs) does not show gate counts; only the normal status does.
mistakes: My first draft of the ordering test expected clippy (2 ends, 2 overruled) before test (3 ends, 2 overruled); the sort puts the gate with more ends first on equal overruled counts, so I fixed the test, not the sort.
My first gate chain fixture used a rejected retry, which counted as a second `test` gate and corrupted the expected counts; I switched the not-overruled retries to the failed state.
A test record id used seconds 99 and was out of range; fixed.
I ran `grep` and `tail` through Bash once each; the hook refused them and I used Read/Grep tools instead.
I could not read the saved output of the full cargo test run (outside the working directory), so my pass claim for it rests on the absence of a failure exit code.
learnings: PreventionKind has one non-test exhaustive match (status.rs mistake_report) that the compiler found; no other match on it exists.

IntrospectionRecord uses deny_unknown_fields, so a new typed gate field would have forced edits in many files outside the deliverable list; the `gate` answer field plus a '[gate: NAME] ' prefix on `prevention` avoids that.

A rejected job's gate is the name of a failed, non-pre-existing, non-revert check in its verification; `Records::load_dir` over files written with canonical_path()/to_json() gives a fast unit fixture.

addressing_request treats a cause group as addressed when any request cites any member id, so a relax record in a cause group would hide a code-check cause from the backfill; cause_key returning None for loosening kinds prevents it.
athena-cli integration tests cannot reach athena-core's #[cfg(test)] fixtures, so introspection.rs has its own small job-chain helper.
desires: A way to read a saved tool-result file, or a flag that makes the full test run print only its summary lines, so I could see the per-test summary of the full suite.
A producer-side check that runs the new tests against the pre-change source (the 'fails without the change' demonstration).
